source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.5.1 (Moments of the normal distribution), opening sentence continuing across the page break
source_evidence.observation: The exercise quantifies over each p >= 1 and assumes that X has the standard normal distribution N(0,1).
The source states the exact identity ||X||_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) = sqrt(2) [Gamma((1+p)/2) / Gamma(1/2)]^(1/p).
The source additionally asks for the asymptotic conclusion ||X||_{L^p} = O(sqrt(p)) as p tends to infinity.

contract_plain_english: For every exponent p >= 1 and every random variable X with the standard normal distribution N(0,1), the exercise requires the exact L^p-norm formula ||X||_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) = sqrt(2) [Gamma((1+p)/2) / Gamma(1/2)]^(1/p). It then separately requires deducing that this norm is O(sqrt(p)) as p tends to infinity. [PDF pages 12-13 / printed pages 23-24, Exercise 2.5.1 and display (2.11)]
